title: Prometheus
description: The two Prometheus replicas on mon01/mon02: health checks, TSDB head and storage against the 7 d / 20 GB caps, WAL and compactions, scrape pools, rule groups, remote write to Mimir (HA tracker), Alertmanager notifications, queries and the process. Replica picker.

panels.title: Mimir keeps samples from
panels.description: The replica Mimir's HA tracker accepts right now (cortex_ha_tracker_elected_replica_status); the other one's pushes are accepted and dropped. It fails over when the elected replica sends nothing for 30 s (a ~30 s gap at a failover is normal).

panels.title: HA failovers in range
panels.description: Times the HA tracker switched replica in the time range (the Mimir that counted most). Each one is a restart or stall of the elected Prometheus.

panels.title: Checks
panels.description: Both replicas, whatever the Replica picker says. Mirrors the alert rules TargetDown (up), PrometheusRemoteWriteFailing (failed samples over 10 m), PrometheusRemoteWriteBehind (lag over 300 s) and FilesystemAlmostFull (the backend's root FS, where /prometheus lives). The rest are invariants without an alert: config reload, Mimir still receiving, the TSDB under 80 % of its 20 GB cap (past it Prometheus deletes the oldest blocks before 7 d), no TSDB / rule / scrape failures in the last hour, both Alertmanagers discovered and taking alerts.

panels.title: Samples appended / s
panels.description: Scraped and rule-produced samples written to the head, per replica. The two should match within a few %.

panels.title: Head series
panels.description: Series in the in-memory head block (the last ~2-3 h): the main driver of memory use.

panels.title: Of the 20 GB size cap
panels.description: Blocks + WAL + head chunks against --storage.tsdb.retention.size (20 GB, prometheus_tsdb_retention_limit_bytes). At 100 % the oldest blocks go before they are 7 d old.

panels.title: Local history
panels.description: Age of the oldest sample each replica still holds; a full bar is the 7 d time retention. Longer ranges come from Mimir only (396 d).

panels.title: remote_write lag
panels.description: Newest sample appended minus newest sample sent to Mimir. Alert PrometheusRemoteWriteBehind at 300 s for 10 m.

panels.title: Head series
panels.description: Series in the head block, and those whose last sample is a staleness marker (target or series gone) waiting for the next head compaction to drop them.

panels.title: Series churn
panels.description: New series per minute, and series dropped at head GC (every 2 h, the spikes of 'removed'). A steady high 'created' means a label whose values keep changing (see New series per scrape by job).

panels.title: Head chunks
panels.description: Chunks in the head (up to 120 samples, so about one per series per hour at 30 s) and chunks cut per second.

panels.title: Samples appended by type
panels.description: Floats vs native histograms (none of the exporters here sends native histograms).

panels.title: Samples rejected by the TSDB
panels.description: Samples the head refused: older than the newest of their series (out of order; there is no out_of_order_time_window locally) or older than the head's start. Targets that send their own timestamps (Telegraf, the WLC telemetry) are the usual source.

panels.title: Head time span
panels.description: Time the in-memory head covers: grows to ~3 h, then 2 h of it are written out as a block (the saw tooth). Not dropping back means head compaction is stuck.

panels.title: Disk use vs the 20 GB cap
panels.description: The three parts the size cap counts, per replica; the dashed line is --storage.tsdb.retention.size.

panels.title: Local history vs 7 d
panels.description: Age of the oldest local sample. It climbs until the oldest block is entirely past 7 d, then drops by a block. Retention was cut to 7 d on 2026-11-13; the replicas held more before.

panels.title: Blocks loaded and deleted
panels.description: Persisted blocks (2 h blocks are merged into larger ones, up to 10 % of the retention). 'Deleted by SIZE' means the 20 GB cap, not the 7 d, is removing history.

panels.title: Compactions
panels.description: Head-to-block writes (every 2 h) plus merges of older blocks. Vertical compactions merge overlapping blocks (out-of-order data); normally none.

panels.title: Compaction and head GC duration
panels.description: Over the last hour (both run every 2 h, so a shorter window would mostly be empty).

panels.title: TSDB failures
panels.description: Per hour, only the counters that rose: failed compactions, truncations, checkpoints, WAL writes, corruptions (repaired at start; a corruption means a crash or a full disk).

panels.title: WAL write rate and size
panels.description: Bytes appended to the WAL per second and its size on disk (the head's ~3 h plus the last checkpoint; remote_write replays from it after a Mimir outage).

panels.title: WAL fsync
panels.description: Over the last hour: the WAL is fsynced when a 128 MiB segment closes, a few times an hour. The backends' disks are Ceph RBD, so a slow fsync here is Ceph write latency.

panels.title: WAL checkpoints and truncations
panels.description: After each head compaction the WAL is checkpointed and truncated.

panels.title: Scrape pools
panels.description: Per job: targets in the pool (max of the picked replicas), up/down, samples kept per scrape after relabeling, new series per scrape (10 m average: churn) and the slowest target's last scrape. Up to Slowest are the elected replica's scrapes (Mimir keeps only those).

panels.title: Slowest targets
panels.description: The ten slowest scrapes (elected replica). SNMP walks of the switches and WLCs lead; a scrape that hits its timeout fails and the target reads down (alert TargetDown).

panels.title: Samples per scrape by job
panels.description: Samples each job's targets return per scrape after metric relabeling: who fills the head.

panels.title: New series per scrape by job
panels.description: Series a scrape saw for the first time, per job. Spikes at restarts and deploys are normal; a steady stream is a churning label.

panels.title: Scrape drops and pool problems
panels.description: Per hour, only the counters that rose: samples a scrape threw away (over sample_limit, out of order, duplicate timestamps, out of bounds), bodies or label sets over limits, failed scrape pool reloads and target syncs. No job here sets a sample_limit.

panels.title: Scrape interval accuracy (p99)
panels.description: Actual time between two scrapes of a target, p99 per configured interval (10 s pvestatd, 15 s / 30 s the rest). Well above the interval: Prometheus is overloaded or the VM stalled.

panels.title: Service discovery
panels.description: Targets found by service discovery (static_configs only here, so it changes only with a config deploy).

panels.title: Rule groups
panels.description: Each replica evaluates every group itself (the Alertmanager cluster dedupes the alerts). Of interval: last evaluation time against the group's interval; near 100 % the next run is skipped (Missed, in the time range). Samples: series the group's rules returned. Last run should stay under the interval (30 s).

panels.title: Evaluation time per group
panels.description: The ten slowest group evaluations. The ceph-mixin groups (ceph.yml) and storage-health touch the most series.

panels.title: Evaluations, failures, missed runs
panels.description: Rule evaluations per second; failures (a query error, e.g. many-to-many matching) and missed group runs only show when they happen.

panels.title: Rule evaluation latency (p99)
panels.description: One rule's query and one group's whole run (bucketed: values snap to bucket bounds).

panels.title: Alerts pending / firing
panels.description: Active alerts as the rules produce them (both replicas fire the same ones; this is the elected replica's ALERTS series).

panels.title: Samples in / sent
panels.description: Samples read from the WAL into the queue and samples sent to Mimir (10.13.11.103:8080), per second. Both replicas send everything; Mimir keeps the elected one's.

panels.title: Failed / retried
panels.description: Failed: Mimir answered 4xx and the batch was dropped (alert PrometheusRemoteWriteFailing). Retried: 5xx, 429 or a connection error (VIP failover, Mimir restart), sent again. Enqueue retries: the queue was full.

defaults.noValue: No failed or retried sends in range

panels.title: Lag behind the newest sample
panels.description: Newest sample appended minus newest sample sent. Grows while Mimir is unreachable and drains from the WAL afterwards; alert PrometheusRemoteWriteBehind above the dashed line for 10 m.

targets.expr: max by (host) (prometheus_remote_storage_highest_timestamp_in_seconds{job="prometheus", host=~"$host"} - ignoring(remote_name, url) group_right prometheus_remote_storage_queue_highest_sent_timestamp_seconds{job="prometheus", host=~"$host"})

panels.title: Queue: pending samples and bytes
panels.description: Samples buffered in the shards against their capacity (running shards × 10000), and the compressed bytes per second on the wire.

panels.title: Shards
panels.description: Parallel senders. Prometheus scales between min and max_shards (10) by itself; desired above running for long means the queue can't keep up.

panels.title: Send latency and WAL reader
panels.description: Time to push one batch (up to 2000 samples) to Mimir, p99; and how many WAL segments the remote_write reader trails the TSDB (0 normally; climbs during a long outage).

targets.expr: max by (host) (prometheus_tsdb_wal_segment_current{job="prometheus", host=~"$host"}) - max by (host) (prometheus_wal_watcher_current_segment{job="prometheus", host=~"$host"})

panels.title: Replica Mimir keeps
panels.description: The HA tracker's choice over time: the green bar moving is a replica failover.

panels.title: Mimir: newest sample age, standby samples dropped
panels.description: Mimir's end of the pipe: age of the newest sample its distributors received (scrape interval + send delay, normally under a minute) and the standby replica's samples it drops per second.

panels.title: Alerts sent per Alertmanager
panels.description: Each replica sends every alert to both Alertmanagers (mon01 10.13.11.30, mon02 10.13.11.31 :9093), which dedupe them over their gossip cluster. Errors and drops only show when they happen.

panels.title: Notification queue
panels.description: Alerts waiting to be sent (normally 0). A full queue drops alerts.

panels.title: Notification latency (p99)
panels.description: Time to post a batch of alerts to each Alertmanager.

panels.title: Query engine latency (p99)
panels.description: Per phase: queue_time (waiting for a slot), prepare_time (selecting series), inner_eval (the PromQL). Local queries are the rules plus Explore on prometheus-mon01/02; the dashboards query Mimir.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, host, slice) (rate(prometheus_engine_query_duration_histogram_seconds_bucket{job="prometheus", host=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Concurrent queries and samples loaded
panels.description: Queries in flight against --query.max-concurrency (20), and samples the engine loaded per second.

panels.title: HTTP API by handler
panels.description: Requests to each Prometheus: /metrics is the replicas scraping each other; /api/v1/query and /targets come from Grafana's per-replica datasources and lylat-obs.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU seconds per second (1 = one core).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory grows with head series; next GC is the heap size at which Go collects next.

panels.title: Goroutines and file descriptors
panels.description: Goroutines grow with targets and remote_write shards; open fds are block files, the WAL and connections.

panels.title: Go GC pause (max)
panels.description: Longest stop-the-world GC pause in the recent window.

panels.title: Warnings and errors per replica
panels.description: Prometheus' own WARN/ERROR lines. The journal marks every container line as priority 'error', so this matches level= in the text.

panels.title: Prometheus warnings and errors
panels.description: TSDB, remote_write, rule and notifier problems (failed scrapes are not logged).

panels.title: Prometheus log
panels.description: All lines: compactions ('write block'), WAL checkpoints, config reloads ('Completed loading of configuration file').
